senses.gloss: शिमिक शिमिक, N. of a district in Kaśmīra.

सीमिक सीमिक, अस्, m. (in Uṇādi-s. II. 43.
said to be fr. rt. स्यम्), a kind of tree; an ant-hill
(= स्यमीक); an ant or similar small insect.
सीमीक, अस्, m. a kind of tree; [cf. सीमिक above.]

शिमी शिमी, f., Ved. power, strength, (Sāy.
= शक्ति, Ṛg-veda 1. 151, 1); a sacrificial rite,
ceremony (= कर्म, Naigh. II. 7).
—शिमी-वत्,
आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. possessed of power, full of energy
or strength, strong, vigorous, energetic; granting
desires, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda 1. 155, 2.
शिमीवतोः = इष्ट-प्रदानादि-कर्मवतोः or प्र-
हरणादि-कर्मवतोः.)

शिमृडी शिमृडी, f. a kind of shrub (=
बल्या).

शिम्ब शिम्ब, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 1. शि),
a sort of large shrub, = चक्र-मर्दक; (आ), f. a
pod, legume, (also written सिम्बा.)

सिम्बा सिम्बा, f. (also written शिम्बा, q. v.),
a pod, &c.

शिम्बल, अम्, n., Ved. the flower of the Śalmalī
tree, (Sāy. = शल्मली-कुसुम, Ṛg-veda III. 53, 22.)

शिम्बि, इस्, f. a pod, legume [cf. सिम्बि]; a kind
of grass (= एरका).
—शिम्बि-पर्णी or शिम्बि-पर्-
णिका, f. a sort of kidney-bean, Phaseolus Trilobus
(= मुद्ग-पर्णी).

शिम्बी, f. a pod, legume; a sort of kidney-bean;
a kind of plant (= कपि-कच्छु).

सिम्बि, इस्, f. a pod (= शिम्बि).
—सिम्बि-जा, f.
‘pod-born,’ any pulse or grain growing in pods.
सिम्बी, f. = शिम्बी.

शिम्बिक, अस्, m. a sort of pulse or kidney-bean,
= कृष्ण-मुद्ग; (आ), f. a pod, legume.

शिम्बाता शिम्बाता, m. du., Ved. mentioned
in Naigh. III. 6. together with शत-रा and शात-
पन्ता among the सुख-नामानि, see Ṛg-veda X.
105, 5; [cf. शातपन्ता.]

शिम्यु शिम्यु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. arousing, ex-
citing, (Sāy. = बोधमान, Ṛg-veda VII. 18, 5);
(उस्), m. an evil demon, Rākṣasa, (according to
Sāy. = शमयितृ = बध-कारिन्, ‘a destroyer,’
Ṛg-veda I. 100, 18.)
शीम शीम in सु-शीम, q. v.

सिम सिम, अस्, आ, अम्, (in Uṇādi-s. I. 143.
said to be fr. rt. सि; probably connected with
1. सम; सिमस्मात्, abl. c. = सर्वस्मात्, Ṛg-
veda I. 95, 7; सिमस्मै, dat. c. everywhere, Ṛg-
veda 1. 115, 4), all, every, whole, entire; (अस्), m.,
Ved. ‘the best, most excellent,’ epithet of Indra,
(in Ṛg-veda VIII. 4, 1. सिमा, voc. c. = सिम =
श्रेष्ठेन्द्र); (आ), f., Ved. a cord, band, (accord-
ing to some अस्, m.; cf. सीमा.)
—सिमा-त्व, अम्,
n., Ved. the state of a cord.

सीमा, f. a boundary, bound, border, limit, &c.
(= सीमन् above).
—सीमाज्ञान (˚मा-अज्˚), अम्, n.
ignorance of boundaries.
—सीमाधिप (˚मा-अध्˚),
अस्, m. a neighbouring king.
—सीमा-निश्चय, अस्,
m. a legal decision with respect to landmarks and
boundaries.
—सीमान्त (˚मा-अन्˚), अस्, m. a boun-
dary-line, frontier-line, border, boundary.
—सी-
[]
मान्त-पूजन, अम्, n. the act of honouring a
village boundary, &c.
—सीमा-लिङ्ग, अम्, n. a boun-
dary-mark, landmark.
—सीमा-वाद, अस्, m. a dispute
about boundaries.
—सीमा-विनिर्णय, अस्, m. the
(legal) decision of disputed questions about boun-
daries and landmarks.
—सीमा-विवाद, अस्, m. liti-
gation about boundaries.
—सीमा-विवाद-धर्म,
अस्, m. the law respecting disputes about boundaries.
—सीमा-वृक्ष, अस्, m. ‘boundary-tree,’ a tree
serving as a boundary-mark.
—सीमा-सन्धि, इस्, m.
‘boundary-junction,’ the meeting of two boundaries.
—सीमा-सेतु-विनिर्णय, अस्, m. (legal) decision
about boundaries and barriers.
—सीमोल्लङ्घन
(˚मा-उल्˚), अम्, n. the leaping over or transgressing
boundaries, passing a frontier.

सिम् सिम्, ind. (in Vedic grammar) a tech-
nical term for the eight simple vowels (viz. अ, आ, इ,
ई, उ, ऊ, ऋ, ॠ).

सीम् सीम्, ind., Ved. a particle laying stress
on a preceding word (= इद्); everywhere, on all
sides (= सर्वतस्, Ṛg-veda II. 28, 4, IV. 56, 1).

सिमिसिमाय सिमिसिमाय (fr. an imitative
sound), Nom. P. सिमिसिमायति, &c., to tremble,
quiver, be convulsed.
सिम्भ् सिम्भ्. See rt. सिभ्, col. 1.

सीमन् सीमन्, आ, f. (according to some also
m., but only f. according to Amara and Vopa-deva
IV. 3; according to others also n. in Ved.; in
Uṇādi-s. IV. 150. said to be fr. rt. सि; in some
senses perhaps connected with rt. सिव्), a boundary,
border, bound, limit, margin, frontier; a mound or
ridge or anything serving to mark the boundary of
a field, village, &c.; a mark, landmark (in general);
a bank, shore, coast; the horizon; a suture (of the
skull &c.; cf. सीवन); the bounds of morality or
decorum, keeping within bounds, rectitude; a field;
the nape of the neck; the scrotum.

सीमन्त, अस्, m. (for सीमान्त, i. e. सीमन् or
सीमा + अन्त), a boundary-line, (see सीमान्त under
सीमा); a separation or parting of the hair on
each side of the head so as to leave a line; a land-
mark; N. of a son of king Bhadra-sena; of a poet;
(अस्, अम्), m. n. the head (according to some).
—सी-
मन्त-करण, अम्, n. the act or ceremony of part-
ing the hair.
—सीमन्तोन्नयन (˚त-उन्˚), अम्,
n. ‘arranging the parting of the hair,’ N. of one of
the twelve Saṃskāras or purificatory rites, (it is ob-
served by women in the fourth, sixth, or eighth
month of their pregnancy; see under संस्-कार,
p. 1041.)

सीमन्तक, अस्, m., N. of a particular kind of
infernal being or inhabitant of hell; (अम्), n. red
lead (with which a mark is sometimes made along
the division of the hair).

सीमन्तय, Nom. P. सीमन्तयति, &c., to mark
by a line, part (as hair &c.).

सीमन्तित, अस्, आ, अम्, marked by a line, parted
(as hair &c.).

सीमन्तिनी, f. ‘having hair-parting,’ a woman;
N. of a daughter of king Citra-varman.

सीमन्त्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, being parted or
divided.
